provider.provenance_chain: College Basketball Reference (sports-reference.com/cbb) team game-log tables -> LogScraperScript.R (the repo's own 'CBB team game log scraper', documented in the same repo's sports-data-catalog.html with source sports-reference.com/cbb, method 'HTML table scraping') -> per-season logs{year}.csv committed in this repo under sportsdatafiles/. In-data provenance: every per-season row carries CBR's own school-page URL (/cbb/schools/<slug>/men/<year>.html) and CBR's signature SRS/SOS columns.
provider.pull_route: raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit SHA (commit-addressed, not branch-addressed)

pin_rule: repo + commit SHA + path + git blob SHA + asset size + SHA-256 of the pulled bytes, recorded in this manifest together with the pull timestamp (retrieved_at_utc). Unlike the PR #2867 rolling release, this pin is COMMIT-ANCHORED: the raw URLs are addressed by the full commit SHA, so upstream bytes cannot drift under the pin without the commit changing; the committed pull script re-downloads at the pinned commit and refuses any size/hash/blob drift as SOURCE_CHANGED_AFTER_SNAPSHOT. Scope discipline: logs1520.csv is admitted for 2014-15 -> 2017-18 ONLY (see its excluded_rows_in_file); the merged cbblogs1521.csv / cbblogs1522.csv composites are NOT admitted (rejected_sources).

excluded_rows_in_file.exclusion_reason: 2018-19 rows are INCOMPLETE (stop 2019-03-24, late tournament missing) and 2019-20 rows duplicate the logs20.csv season (whose count differs by 2 rows: 11,095 vs 11,097 here); both seasons are admitted from their per-season files instead. Reading logs1520.csv outside its admitted seasons is off-pin.

satisfies.pr_2866_precondition_c_cbr_leg: YES — on merge of this PR. The CBR season-schedule leg of the design section 2 three-way fixture agreement is pinned here by full tuple from a lawful, provenance-documented mirror, so precondition (c) of the CBB_TORVIK_EFFICIENCY_V1 design screen (PR #2843 section 3; records PR #2866 and PR #2870) is SATISFIABLE and the section 3 screen may run exactly as designed, reading the CBR leg from these pinned bytes under source_id CBR_SCHEDULE_MIRROR_MATTWAITE_V1 with the design's SCHEDULE_DISCREPANCY logging unchanged.
satisfies.three_way_proof: derive_three_way_proof.py + three_way_proof_result.json in this packet: fixtures derived from the pinned CBR bytes (mirror-deduped) agree three ways on a declared 27-fixture sample (every season: championship game + early/mid probe-date fixtures; 2019-20 substitutes a late-probe fixture — no championship game exists, COVID-19 cancellation). Result at admission (verified-by-pull): 27/27 AGREE, 0 SCHEDULE_DISCREPANCY; the derivation paired 48,155 fixtures across the nine seasons with 0 mirror-inconsistent pairs; every input byte stream was hash-verified against its pin (this manifest for CBR, PR #2867's for hoopR) before use, and each Torvik morning-of file sits at the PR #2832 pinned commit.

identity_note: Unchanged from PR #2835 / PR #2867: the ESPN/Torvik/NCAA identity crosswalk is OPEN and NOT admitted. This manifest pins CBR-mirror bytes only. The design screen's own audited, design-evidence-only name-join (PR #2843 section 2) remains the only expedient; the proof's normalization (CBR school slugs + the published NORMALIZATION_OVERRIDES table + published mirror-inference resolutions) is part of that expedient and admits no identity mapping.
known_limitations: ROW UNIT: each CBR file logs one row per team per game (~2 rows per D1-vs-D1 fixture, 1 row when the opponent is non-D1). Fixtures must be derived by mirror dedupe before any agreement check; raw counts are team-rows, not games.

NAME VARIANTS exist inside CBR itself ('UNC' vs 'North Carolina', 'Connecticut' vs hoopR's 'UConn') and logs1520.csv uses full mascot names in its Team column where the per-season files use school names. The proof's normalization is explicit and table-driven (NORMALIZATION_OVERRIDES in derive_three_way_proof.py, ~40 entries, published in three_way_proof_result.json); surfaces resolved by mirror inference are published per season in the same result file.

AUTHORIZATION: the mirror asserts no license and no Sports Reference authorization; it is a university professor's long-standing public teaching dataset (last-touch commits 2020-12-28 -> 2024-04-10). This record's posture: factual game data (dates, teams, scores), read-only, internal verification only, hash-pinned, never redistributed.

SCORE-MISSING ROWS: the pinned bytes contain rows with non-numeric scores (2 in the 2014-15 scope of logs1520.csv, 58 in logs23.csv) — unplayed/postponed entries in CBR's logs. The derivation counts and excludes them; they can form no fixture and are never silently resolved.
2019-20 HAS NO CHAMPIONSHIP GAME (COVID-19 cancellation; CBR logs end 2020-03-11). The proof's sample for that season is three regular-season fixtures, declared as such.
